Title: Diagnosis of test `org.apache.commons.csv.CSVParserTest.testDuplicateHeaderEntries`

Details:
The test `testDuplicateHeaderEntries` uses `CSVParser.parse` to parse a CSV string with header `"a,b,a"`, but also supplies an empty header array via the format (`CSVFormat.DEFAULT.withHeader(new String[]{})`). According to the test annotation, this should throw an `IllegalStateException`.

Examining the code:

- The `CSVParser.parse(String, CSVFormat)` method simply creates a new `CSVParser` instance with a `StringReader` and the format.
- The `CSVParser` constructor performs `format.validate()` and then calls `initializeHeader()` to set up the header map.
- The `CSVFormat.validate()` method, when a header array is defined (not null), checks for duplicate header names and throws an `IllegalStateException` if duplicates are found (lines 650-655). It compares the length of the header array to the size of a Set built from the header names to detect duplicates.
- However, in this test, the header passed to the format is an empty array (`new String[]{}`).
- The `CSVParser.initializeHeader()` method then reads the header from the input if the format header array is empty (length == 0). It reads the first record `"a,b,a"` from the CSV content as the header.
- It then builds a `LinkedHashMap` mapping header names to indices (lines 369-373).
- During this header map build, it uses `Map.put()` to insert each header name. A `Map` will overwrite existing keys, so the duplicate "a" keys will override the previous mapping silently (no exception here).
- Notably, `CSVFormat.validate()` only checks duplicate headers if the header array defined on the format is not null and not empty.
- When the header is empty (length 0), the duplicates in the actual CSV header line are not checked at `validate()` but rather silently stored in the map during `initializeHeader()`.

As a result, no exception is thrown despite duplicate headers in the input CSV's header line because the duplicate header detection logic in `CSVFormat.validate()` does not apply to header lines inferred from the CSV input (empty header array case). The `initializeHeader()` method silently overwrites duplicate header keys, failing to detect the duplicates and causing the test expecting an `IllegalStateException` to fail.

In summary, the bug arises because duplicate detection is only performed on the header array provided by `CSVFormat` but not on headers read from the CSV data itself in `initializeHeader()`.

The fix should involve adding duplicate header detection in `CSVParser.initializeHeader()` when reading headers from the CSV input (i.e., when `formatHeader.length == 0`), throwing an `IllegalStateException` if duplicates are found.

---

Next, I will show the relevant code snippets of `initializeHeader` around header map construction and duplicate detection point, to confirm where exactly to add the fix.

messages.content:
The code snippet of `CSVParser.initializeHeader()` shows:

- When `formatHeader.length == 0`, headers are read from the first CSV record (`nextRecord.values()`).
- A map `hdrMap` is initialized.
- Then header names are put into `hdrMap` by iteration.

Currently, no check occurs in this method to verify if the header array has duplicates before populating the map. Simply using `Map.put()` silently overwrites duplicate keys.

The duplicate header detection code in `CSVFormat.validate()` relies on comparing the length of the header array to the size of the Set made from the header array.

To fix the bug, we should apply similar detection logic within `initializeHeader()` when the header is read from the CSV file (when `formatHeader.length == 0`), for example:

- Build a Set while iterating the header array.
- If a duplicate is found (already in the Set), throw `IllegalStateException` with a message indicating duplicate header names.

This will ensure that duplicates in headers read from the file are detected and throw the expected exception.

---

Suggested method for fix:
- `CSVParser.initializeHeader()` to add duplicate header name detection when the header is read from the CSV input.

---

Methods relevant to this bug and candidate for fix:
- `CSVParser.initializeHeader()`
- Possibly `CSVFormat.validate()` if related changes needed (but the main issue is missing check in `initializeHeader()`).

---
